In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

grandparental childcare is not a simple reflection of the individual characteristics of the grandparent, the parent, or the child but is also strongly influenced by the context in which the grandparents live.
grandparental childcare is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon that is shaped by a variety of individual and contextual factors.

intensive grandparental child care is a complex issue that cannot be fully explained by individual characteristics and that the contextual-structural factors, in addition to cultural factors, play an important role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of grandparental childcare in the family life course is strongly influenced by national policies and attitudes towards work and family.
intensive grandparental care in Europe is largely driven by the availability of other forms of childcare.

the extent to which grandparental childcare is provided is strongly associated with the extent to which mothers are in paid work, and that this relationship is mediated by the extent to which formal childcare is provided.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the extent to which grandparental childcare is used in Europe is not simply a reflection of demographic and socio-economic differences, but is also associated with contextual factors, such as the availability of formal childcare and the labor force participation of older women.
grandparental childcare is not a private, individual decision.
policies that encourage older women to remain employed and that provide formal childcare may have an important impact on grandchildcare, and hence on the employment and well-being of women in Europe.
